I've been working this land for 40 years in Quzhou, and I know its rhythms. My 8 mu runs a tight wheat-maize rotation — the same ground does both seasons. With only two of us in the household, I can't afford mistakes, but I also can't afford to be timid. My well gives me control over water that dry-land farmers don't have, and I use that advantage.

**Wheat (winter):** I'll plant in mid-October after summer maize is off. I've switched to the Jimai improved semi-dwarf varieties — they lodge less and respond well to my fertilizer inputs. I split my nitrogen: base at planting, topdress at jointing. Three irrigations is what this crop needs here — pre-sowing to ensure germination, jointing, and heading. I've seen too many neighbors skip the heading water and lose grain weight. Three pesticide passes: herbicide in early winter, fungicide at heading to hold off fusarium, and aphid spray before harvest. I'll rotary till after maize to incorporate that stubble. Five hundred kg/mu is what I expect.

**Maize (summer):** Right after wheat comes off in June, I go straight in with no-till direct seeding. I won't waste days plowing in the summer heat — the window to June maize is short. I use Zhengdan 958 hybrid; I know exactly how it performs on my ground. Nitrogen goes in two shots — base and topdress at big bell stage. I water twice unless the rains cooperate, at sowing establishment and again at tasseling. Two pesticide applications: pre-emergence herbicide and one pass for corn borer. Six hundred kg/mu is realistic for me.
